rows.question: When does my maternity leave start if my due date is 15 November 2026?
rows.reply:
Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) before the birth covers the last six weeks before the expected delivery date. The law says the employer may not employ a pregnant woman "in den letzten sechs Wochen vor der Entbindung" (in the last six weeks before the delivery). This is called the "Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung" (protection period before the delivery). The exception is if she expressly declares she is willing to work, and she can withdraw that declaration at any time for the future.

The period is counted from the expected delivery date shown in a doctor's or midwife's certificate: "der voraussichtliche Tag der Entbindung ... wie er sich aus dem ärztlichen Zeugnis oder dem Zeugnis einer Hebamme oder eines Entbindungspflegers ergibt". So the date on that certificate is what counts, not a date worked out elsewhere. If the baby is not born on that day, the period before the birth becomes shorter or longer to match.

The excerpts do not set out how the exact first calendar day is counted, so this answer does not fix a start date. Your employer applies the period, based on the certificate.

After the birth, the protection period runs until eight weeks after delivery. It extends to twelve weeks in three cases:
- premature births
- multiple births
- where a disability of the child is medically established before the eight weeks end. In this case only if the woman applies.

If the birth comes early, the period after the birth is also extended by the time lost before it.

The Mutterschutz law does not cover self-employed women. The official family portal says self-employed women are outside the scope of the Mutterschutzgesetz and need to make their own provision for the time before and after the birth.

rows.question: How long after birth can we apply for Elterngeld without losing money?
rows.reply:
The law limits how far back Elterngeld (parental allowance) is paid. It does not phrase this as an application deadline. BEEG §7(1) says Elterngeld is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month of life in which the application is received: "rückwirkend nur für die letzten drei Lebensmonate vor Beginn des Lebensmonats geleistet, in dem der Antrag auf Elterngeld eingegangen ist". These are months of the child's life, counted from the birth, not calendar months.

The consequence is that months of the child's life falling more than three months before the month your application arrives are not paid. For example, an application received during the child's fourth month of life still reaches back to the first month of life. An application received later loses the earliest months.

Elterngeld can be drawn from the day of birth. Basiselterngeld can be drawn until the child completes the 14th month of life. ElterngeldPlus can be drawn until the child completes the 32nd month of life, as long as at least one parent takes it in consecutive months from the 15th month of life (BEEG §4(1)). The application must be made in writing: "Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen" (BEEG §7(1)).

Which months are paid in your case, and how much, is decided by the Elterngeldstelle for your district.

rows.question: How much notice do I have to give my employer for Elternzeit?
rows.reply:
For Elternzeit (parental leave (unpaid job-protected leave)), BEEG §16(1) sets two notice periods, depending on when the leave falls:

- Leave up to the child's third birthday: at least seven weeks before the leave starts ("spätestens sieben Wochen ... vor Beginn der Elternzeit").
- Leave between the third birthday and the end of the child's eighth year: at least 13 weeks before the leave starts ("spätestens 13 Wochen").

You request the leave from your employer in text form ("in Textform vom Arbeitgeber verlangen"). The Familienportal explains that text form can be, for example, a letter without a signature or an email.

When you request leave for the period up to the third birthday, you must also state at the same time which periods within two years you will take as Elternzeit ("für welche Zeiten innerhalb von zwei Jahren Elternzeit genommen werden soll"). If the mother's Elternzeit follows directly after her Mutterschutz period, that period counts towards the two years.

There are two exceptions in the statute:

- Where there are urgent reasons, a reasonable shorter period is possible as an exception ("Bei dringenden Gründen ist ausnahmsweise eine angemessene kürzere Frist möglich").
- If a mother cannot request Elternzeit in time for it to start directly after the maternity protection period, for a reason that is not her fault, she can make the request within one week after that reason ends (BEEG §16(2)).

Your employer must confirm the Elternzeit to you in writing ("Der Arbeitgeber hat ... die Elternzeit zu bescheinigen").

Related: protection against dismissal starts from the time Elternzeit is requested. It starts at the earliest eight weeks before leave up to the third birthday, and at the earliest 14 weeks before leave between the third and eighth birthdays (BEEG §18(1)).

Whether a shorter period is reasonable in your case is not set out in the excerpts. In a dispute with your employer, this is a matter of employment law, and the excerpts do not name the body that decides it.

rows.question: How long is maternity protection after the birth if the baby comes early?
rows.reply:
Under Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period), your employer may not employ you until eight weeks after the birth ("bis zum Ablauf von acht Wochen nach der Entbindung"). An early birth can lengthen this in two separate ways.

1. Birth before the expected date. Before the birth, protection covers the six weeks before the expected date of delivery. If the baby comes before that date, this pre-birth period is shorter. The law adds the shortened time to the period after the birth: "Bei vorzeitiger Entbindung verlängert sich die Schutzfrist nach der Entbindung ... um den Zeitraum der Verkürzung der Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung." For example, if the baby arrives ten days early, the post-birth period runs ten days longer than it otherwise would.

2. Extension to twelve weeks. The post-birth period becomes twelve weeks in three cases:
- premature births ("bei Frühgeburten");
- multiple births ("bei Mehrlingsgeburten");
- when a doctor determines a disability in the child, within the meaning of § 2(1) sentence 1 SGB IX, before the end of the eight weeks after the birth. In this case the extension applies only if the mother applies for it ("nur, wenn die Frau dies beantragt"). The Familienportal says this application is made to the health insurance fund (Krankenkasse).

The two rules combine. If a birth counts as premature and also came before the expected date, the twelve weeks are extended by the days lost from the pre-birth period.

The excerpt from the statute does not define "Frühgeburt". The Familienportal gives one example of a birth that counts medically as premature: a baby weighing less than 2,500 grams at birth. A baby born only a few days early is not automatically a "Frühgeburt". In that case the post-birth period stays at eight weeks, plus the days lost before the birth.

The twelve-week extension does not apply to a stillbirth ("Satz 2 gilt nicht bei einer Totgeburt").

rows.question: Can my employer dismiss me while I am pregnant?
rows.reply:
In general, no. Under § 17 MuSchG, Kündigungsschutz (protection against dismissal) means a dismissal by the employer is not permitted ("Die Kündigung gegenüber einer Frau ist unzulässig") in three periods:
1. During the pregnancy.
2. Until four months after a miscarriage after the twelfth week of pregnancy.
3. Until the end of the protection period after the birth, and at least until four months after the birth.

This protection applies if the employer knew of the pregnancy, miscarriage or birth at the time of dismissal, or is told within two weeks after the dismissal is received ("innerhalb von zwei Wochen nach Zugang der Kündigung"). Missing the two weeks does no harm if the delay was not the woman's fault and she informs the employer without delay. The guidance page adds that the protection applies even if you did not yet know you were pregnant, but you must already have been pregnant when you received the dismissal.

There is one exception. In special cases not connected with the woman's condition during pregnancy, after a miscarriage or after the birth, "die für den Arbeitsschutz zuständige oberste Landesbehörde oder die von ihr bestimmte Stelle" may exceptionally declare the dismissal permissible. Such a dismissal must be in writing and must state the reason. The guidance page gives examples of such cases: insolvency of the company, partial closure of the business, a small business that cannot continue without a qualified replacement, or a particularly serious breach of duty. It also says that without the authority's consent the dismissal is invalid ("unwirksam").

If you are dismissed without that consent, the guidance page says you must bring a claim before the competent labour court ("Klage vor dem zuständigen Arbeitsgericht"), normally within 3 weeks of receiving the written dismissal ("normalerweise innerhalb von 3 Wochen ... ab Erhalt der schriftlichen Kündigung"). If no claim is brought, the dismissal is treated as valid. The page also says you should involve the competent supervisory authority. Challenging the authority's consent does not replace the claim before the labour court.

If you take Elternzeit after the birth, the protection can be extended under § 18 BEEG.

Whether a particular dismissal is permitted is not something this service can assess. That is decided by the labour court and, for the exception, by the supervisory authority responsible for maternity protection in your state.

rows.question: Is there an income limit above which we get no Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under BEEG §1(8), the right to Elterngeld (parental allowance) lapses ("Ein Anspruch entfällt") if the entitled person had a zu versteuerndes Einkommen (taxable income) of more than 175,000 euros in the last completed tax assessment period before the child's birth ("im letzten abgeschlossenen Veranlagungszeitraum vor der Geburt des Kindes").

If another person also meets the conditions, for example the other parent living in the same household with the child, the limit applies to both incomes added together. The right lapses if "die Summe des zu versteuernden Einkommens beider Personen mehr als 175 000 Euro beträgt".

The limit refers to taxable income, not gross income. The official Familienportal explains that taxable income is usually much lower than gross income, because certain deductions are subtracted. It also says the Finanzamt determines your taxable income, and that figure appears in your tax assessment (Steuerbescheid).

If the tax assessment for that year is not yet available when you apply, BEEG §8 still allows payment. If the information in the application indicates the limit will probably not be exceeded, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation in case the limit turns out to be exceeded. If it cannot yet be stated whether the limit is exceeded, the decision on the amount is provisional until the required information is provided.

The 175,000 euro figure is the current statutory rule. The official guidance page describes different limits for earlier births. The statutory transitional provision that governs earlier births is not among the sources I have, so I cannot say which limit applies to a particular birth date.

Whether the limit applies to your family, and which version of it, is decided by the Elterngeldstelle for your district.

rows.question: How many months of Elterngeld can we get in total?
rows.reply:
The law sets the number of months by type of Elterngeld (parental allowance). It does not set one fixed total.

Basic months. Parents together are entitled to 12 monthly payments of basic Elterngeld: "Die Eltern haben gemeinsam Anspruch auf zwölf Monatsbeträge Basiselterngeld" (BEEG §4(3)). They are jointly entitled to two further months, the partner months, if one parent's earned income is reduced in two months of the child's life: "zwei weitere Monate Basiselterngeld (Partnermonate)" (BEEG §4(3)).

Elterngeld Plus. Instead of one month of basic Elterngeld, a parent can take two months of Elterngeld Plus (BEEG §4(3)).

Limits per parent. One parent can receive at most 12 monthly payments of basic Elterngeld, plus at most four monthly payments of the partnership bonus under §4b (BEEG §4(4)). A parent is only entitled to Elterngeld if they receive it for at least two months of the child's life (BEEG §4(4)). The official guidance page says each parent can get up to 4 additional months of Elterngeld Plus as a partnership bonus if both work part-time at the same time (familienportal.de).

Time limits. Basic Elterngeld can be received until the child completes the 14th month of life. Elterngeld Plus can be received until the child completes the 32nd month of life, as long as at least one parent takes it in consecutive months from the 15th month onward (BEEG §4(1)). Elterngeld is paid for months of the child's life, not calendar months (BEEG §4(2)).

Premature births. The joint entitlement to basic Elterngeld is higher if the child was born early, measured from the expected date of delivery on the doctor's or midwife's certificate (BEEG §4(5)):
- at least 6 weeks early: 13 monthly payments
- at least 8 weeks early: 14 monthly payments
- at least 12 weeks early: 15 monthly payments
- at least 16 weeks early: 16 monthly payments
In these cases, the per-parent maximum and the age limits for basic Elterngeld rise as well (BEEG §4(5)).

This is the general rule. How many months your family receives depends on your situation, and only the authority responsible for Elterngeld decides that. Approach the Elterngeld office for your district.

rows.question: What is the Partnerschaftsbonus and who qualifies?
rows.reply:
The Partnerschaftsbonus (partnership bonus months) is a set of additional monthly amounts of parental allowance for parents who both work part-time in the same months. It is paid in the extended form of parental allowance, where one month of basic allowance can be taken as two months instead (BEEG §4 (3)).

What the law requires (BEEG §4b):
- Both parents must work "nicht weniger als 24 und nicht mehr als 32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats". That means at least 24 and at most 32 hours a week, averaged over that month of the child's life.
- Both parents must also meet the general conditions for parental allowance in § 1 of the act. The excerpts do not set out what § 1 requires.
- If both conditions are met, each parent is entitled to one additional monthly amount for that month.
- Each parent can receive at most four monthly amounts. The bonus can only be taken for at least two months of the child's life.
- The parents can only take it at the same time and in consecutive months of the child's life.
- The consecutive-months requirement still counts as met if it later turns out that the conditions were not present in every month for which the bonus was claimed (§4b (5)).

One parent alone (BEEG §4c (2)): a parent can receive these additional months alone if they work 24 to 32 hours a week on average in at least two and at most four consecutive months, and one of these three grounds applies:
1. The parent meets the conditions for the tax relief for single parents under § 24b (1) and (3) of the Income Tax Act, and the other parent lives neither with them nor with the child.
2. Care by the other parent would endanger the child's welfare within the meaning of § 1666 (1) and (2) of the Civil Code.
3. Care by the other parent is impossible, in particular because of serious illness or severe disability. Economic reasons and being busy with other activities do not count.

If one of these grounds arises while both parents are already receiving the bonus, one parent can continue receiving it alone (BEEG §4b (4)).

On the amount, the official family portal says the bonus is calculated in the same way as the extended form of parental allowance. It also says the bonus is between 150 and 900 euros a month per parent, depending on income before the birth.

Whether you qualify, and for how much, is decided only by your local parental allowance office.

rows.reply:

The official family portal says that when applying retroactively, you state in the application that you are applying retroactively and from when you want to receive Kindergeld. It says the application is submitted to the family benefits office at your local employment agency (Agentur für Arbeit).

Whether you were entitled for those months, and how much is paid, is decided by that family benefits office, not here.

rows.question: How much Kindergeld do we get per month for our first child?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) is 259 euros per month for each child. The statute says: "Das Kindergeld beträgt monatlich für jedes Kind 259 Euro" (EStG §66(1); the same wording appears in BKGG §6(1)). The law sets one figure for each child and does not set a different amount for a first child.

Kindergeld is paid monthly from the start of the month in which the conditions are met, until the end of the month in which they stop being met ("vom Beginn des Monats an gezahlt, in dem die Anspruchsvoraussetzungen erfüllt sind", EStG §66(2)).

This is the amount the law sets. It does not decide whether your family is entitled. Only the Familienkasse decides that. The official family portal links to the online Kindergeld application at the Bundesagentur für Arbeit.

rows.question: How quickly do we have to register the birth at the Standesamt?
rows.reply:
The law requires the birth to be reported to the Standesamt (civil registry office) responsible for the place where the child was born within one week. The Personenstandsgesetz says the birth is to be reported "binnen einer Woche" to the Standesamt "in dessen Zuständigkeitsbereich es geboren ist". The report can come from the persons named in the law, orally or in writing, or in writing from the institutions named in the law. If a child is stillborn, the report must be made "spätestens am dritten auf die Geburt folgenden Werktag", meaning by the third working day after the birth at the latest.

One official checklist describes this as "innerhalb von 7 Werktagen" (within 7 working days). The statute says one week, and the statute governs.

According to the official family portal, if your child is born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the facility notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends the birth certificate from the facility. If your child is born at home, the midwife or doctor issues that certificate, and you must present it to the responsible Standesamt within one week.

If you have not yet decided on a name, the same portal says you must report it to the Standesamt within one month. After that, the Standesamt is obliged to inform the family court.

The Standesamt for the place of birth is the authority for registering the birth. The portal says its website lists any further documents you need.

rows.question: Does my Krankenkasse pay for a midwife?
rows.reply:
The law gives women with statutory health insurance an entitlement to midwife care. Under SGB V §24d, the insured woman is entitled to medical care and to midwife care during pregnancy, at the birth and after the birth. This includes the examinations to confirm the pregnancy and prenatal check-ups.

Midwife care after the birth (the postnatal period) runs until twelve weeks after the birth: "bis zum Ablauf von zwölf Wochen nach der Geburt". Anything beyond that needs a doctor's order: "weitergehende Leistungen bedürfen der ärztlichen Anordnung".

If the mother cannot look after the child after the birth, the insured child has its own entitlement to the midwife care that relates to the child (SGB V §24d).

The Familienportal puts it plainly: every woman with statutory health insurance is entitled to support from a Hebamme (midwife).

Whether a particular service is covered in your case is decided by your Krankenkasse (statutory health insurer). Contact your Krankenkasse about your own situation.

If you have private health insurance, that is outside what this product covers. The Familienportal advises clarifying in advance with your private insurer which services it pays for.

rows.question: How do we insure the baby after the birth?
rows.reply:
Under federal law, a newborn can be covered through Familienversicherung (free family cover for dependants) in statutory health insurance. SGB V §10 says the children of members of a statutory health insurance fund are insured ("Versichert sind ... die Kinder von Mitgliedern") if the child:
1. lives or usually stays in Germany,
2. is not compulsorily or voluntarily insured in their own right,
3. is not exempt from insurance or from compulsory insurance,
4. is not self-employed as a main occupation, and
5. has no total income regularly above one-seventh of the monthly reference value ("ein Siebtel der monatlichen Bezugsgröße").

Children are covered up to age 18. Cover can continue to 23 if the child is not working, and to 25 during school, vocational training or a recognised voluntary year. There is no age limit for a child with a disability who cannot support themselves.

There is an exception that matters when the parents are insured differently. Under §10(3), the child is not covered if the parent who is related to the child, and who is married to or the registered partner of the member, is not a member of a statutory fund, and that parent's total income regularly exceeds one-twelfth of the annual earnings limit ("ein Zwölftel der Jahresarbeitsentgeltgrenze") and is regularly higher than the member's income.

If the conditions are met through more than one parent, the member chooses the fund. The member must report the child to the responsible health insurance fund, with the information needed to run the family cover ("an die zuständige Krankenkasse zu melden"). The national association of health insurance funds sets a uniform reporting procedure and uniform forms.

You will need the birth certificate for this. The family portal lists registration with the health insurance fund ("Anmeldung bei der Krankenkasse") among the things the birth certificate is needed for. The child must be registered within 1 week at the registry office (Standesamt) responsible for the place of birth, and that office issues the birth certificate.

Whether your baby qualifies for family cover is decided by the parent's statutory health insurance fund. If neither parent is in statutory insurance, the excerpts here do not cover how to insure the child. Contact the health insurer of the parent concerned.

rows.question: When are the first check-ups for the baby?
rows.reply:
The first check-ups for children are called U1, U2, U3 and so on. The Kinder-Richtlinie sets ten of these examinations in the first six years of life ("insgesamt zehn Untersuchungen"). Each has a set time window and a wider tolerance limit (Toleranzgrenze).

The first three are:

- U1: immediately after the birth ("Unmittelbar nach der Geburt"). It should be done within the first 30 minutes after the baby is born ("innerhalb der ersten 30 Minuten nach der Geburt"). If no doctor is present at the birth but a midwife is, the midwife should carry it out.
- U2: from the 3rd to the 10th day of life ("3.-10. Lebenstag"). The tolerance limit is the 3rd to the 14th day ("3.-14. Lebenstag").
- U3: in the 4th to 5th week of life ("4.-5. Lebenswoche"). The tolerance limit is the 3rd to the 8th week ("3.-8. Lebenswoche").

The Kinder-Richtlinie says the examinations can only be used within these periods, taking the tolerance limits into account ("können nur in den jeweils angegebenen Zeiträumen unter Berücksichtigung folgender Toleranzgrenzen in Anspruch genommen werden").

If your baby is born early, the same periods still apply ("Auch bei Frühgeborenen sind die Untersuchungszeiträume einzuhalten"). Being born early is taken into account when the results are assessed.

The later check-ups continue up to U9, in the 60th to 64th month of life.

rows.question: What is Mutterschaftsgeld and when do I apply for it?
rows.reply:
Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is a payment for the protection periods before and after the birth and for the day of delivery ("für die Zeit der Schutzfristen vor und nach der Entbindung sowie für den Entbindungstag").

Who pays it depends on your health insurance:

- If you are a member of a statutory health insurer, you receive Mutterschaftsgeld under the rules of the Social Code, Book V (MuSchG §19(1)). Under SGB V §24i(1), it goes to female members who are entitled to sick pay when unable to work, or who receive no pay because of the protection periods. It also goes to women whose employment ends immediately before the protection period begins, if they were a member of a health insurer on the last day of that employment.
- If you are not a member of a statutory health insurer, Mutterschaftsgeld is paid by the federal government, up to 210 euros in total ("insgesamt höchstens 210 Euro"). It is paid on application by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung ("auf Antrag vom Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung gezahlt") (MuSchG §19(2)).

How the amount is set for statutory members in employment:

- It is the average net pay per calendar day from the last three settled calendar months before the protection period starts.
- It is at most 13 euros per calendar day ("höchstens 13 Euro für den Kalendertag") (SGB V §24i(2)).
- The employer pays a supplement covering the difference between 13 euros and that average net daily pay (MuSchG §20(1)).

The right to Mutterschaftsgeld is suspended while you receive contribution-liable pay, earned income or holiday compensation. This does not apply to one-off payments (SGB V §24i(4)).

The federal family portal says the protection periods "beginnen normalerweise 6 Wochen vor dem errechneten Geburtstermin und enden 8 Wochen nach der Geburt" (normally begin 6 weeks before the calculated due date and end 8 weeks after the birth).

When to apply: the excerpts do not say when or how to submit the application to a statutory health insurer, so I cannot give a timing. They do say what payment before the birth depends on. That is a certificate from a doctor or midwife stating the expected date of delivery ("das Zeugnis eines Arztes oder einer Hebamme maßgebend, in dem der voraussichtliche Tag der Entbindung angegeben ist") (SGB V §24i(3)).

For the application route and timing:

- If you are statutorily insured, contact your statutory health insurer.
- If you are not, the excerpts name the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung as the body that pays on application.

Whether you qualify, and how much you would receive, is decided by that body, not here.

rows.question: We are not married. Is my partner automatically the legal father?
rows.reply:
No. Under federal law, a man does not become the legal father simply by being the mother's partner. BGB §1592 names exactly three ways a man becomes the legal father of a child:

1. he is married to the mother at the time of the birth ("zum Zeitpunkt der Geburt mit der Mutter des Kindes verheiratet");
2. he has acknowledged paternity ("die Vaterschaft anerkannt hat"); or
3. a court has established his paternity ("gerichtlich festgestellt").

Where the parents are not married at the birth, the official family portal says the father must make a Vaterschaftsanerkennung (acknowledgement of paternity) to count legally as the father. It also says the acknowledgement is voluntary and requires the mother's consent.

What the statute says about the acknowledgement:
- It can be made before the child is born ("schon vor der Geburt des Kindes zulässig", BGB §1594(4)).
- It is not effective while another man's paternity exists (BGB §1594(2)).
- An acknowledgement made subject to a condition or a time limit is invalid (BGB §1594(3)).
- Its legal effects can only be relied on from the moment it becomes effective (BGB §1594(1)).

Where it is made: the family portal says the father must make the declaration in person at a competent office, for example the youth welfare office, a registry office, a local court or a notary. The mother must also declare her consent in person. The office records both. Depending on the federal state, a notary or local court may charge a fee.

Parental responsibility is a separate step. The family portal says acknowledging paternity does not on its own give the father parental responsibility. That also requires declarations by both parents that they want joint parental responsibility, or a corresponding court decision. Where the parents are not married at the birth, the mother has parental responsibility from the birth. The local youth welfare office advises on parental responsibility.

rows.question: How do unmarried parents get joint custody?
rows.reply:
When parents are not married to each other at the birth, the mother has parental custody alone at first. Under federal law, unmarried parents get joint custody in any of three ways:

1. Both parents declare that they want to take on custody jointly. These are called Sorgeerklärung (declaration of joint custody), in the statute "Sorgeerklärungen".
2. The parents marry each other.
3. The family court transfers custody to both parents jointly.

The statute says that otherwise the mother has custody ("Im Übrigen hat die Mutter die elterliche Sorge").

The other parent must first be legally recognised as the father. This happens when he acknowledges the child as his own with the mother's consent, or when a court establishes paternity. Acknowledging paternity does not by itself give custody. A Sorgeerklärung or a court decision is still needed.

The declarations can be made, for example, at the youth welfare office or before a notary. They can be made before the birth.

On the court route, the family court acts on the application of one parent. It transfers all or part of custody to both parents jointly if this does not go against the child's welfare ("wenn die Übertragung dem Kindeswohl nicht widerspricht"). If the other parent puts forward no reasons against joint custody, and none are otherwise apparent, the law presumes that joint custody does not go against the child's welfare. In that case the official guidance says the court decides in a simplified procedure, without hearing the youth welfare office and without hearing the parents in person.

If jointly responsible parents later separate, joint custody continues.

Your local youth welfare office (Jugendamt) advises on all questions of parental custody. Whether custody is transferred in a particular case is decided by the family court.

rows.question: Where do we apply for Elterngeld in Frankfurt?
rows.reply:
Elterngeld (parental allowance) is handled by an Elterngeldstelle (the state office that decides parental allowance). The law says the responsible office is the one the state has designated for the district where your child has their residence in Germany when the first application is made ("Behörde des Bezirks, in dem das Kind ... zum Zeitpunkt der ersten Antragstellung seinen inländischen Wohnsitz hat"). For a child living in Frankfurt, that means the Elterngeldstelle responsible for Frankfurt.

The federal family portal says you can apply at an Elterngeldstelle in person or online, and that every state offers a digital application. It tells you to contact the Elterngeldstelle responsible for your child's place of residence.

In Hessen, the Regierungspräsidium Gießen Elterngeld page lists contact details for the six Hessian offices for welfare and social affairs ("Hessischen Ämter für Versorgung und Soziales"), and the state's supervisory office for Elterngeld. The excerpts do not say which of the six covers Frankfurt. That page's contact list is where to find it.

The application must be made in writing ("Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen"). Payment is backdated only for the last three months of the child's life before the month your application arrives, so applying late loses whole months of payment.

rows.question: Where do we apply for Elterngeld in Berlin?
rows.reply:
You apply to the Elterngeld (parental allowance) office responsible for your district, the Elterngeldstelle (the state office that decides parental allowance).

Which office is responsible: federal law leaves it to each state to designate the offices. The competent one is the office for the district where the child has their residence in Germany at the time of the first application ("des Bezirks, in dem das Kind ... zum Zeitpunkt der ersten Antragstellung seinen inländischen Wohnsitz hat"). The excerpts do not name the specific Berlin office for each district. Your district's Elterngeldstelle is the authority for this.

How to apply in Berlin: the law says Elterngeld must be applied for in writing ("schriftlich zu beantragen"). The excerpts give two ways in Berlin:
- Online through Service Berlin. To do this you log in with a BundID account, or register for one. Logging in with the online ID function of an electronic ID card or electronic residence permit (eAT) is recommended. An Elster certificate or username and password are alternatives.
- Through ElterngeldDigital, which covers Berlin. A digital assistant helps you fill in the form. You then print it, sign it and post it to your responsible Elterngeldstelle.

Signatures: the application must be signed by the person applying. The other entitled parent also signs to confirm they have seen it. This does not apply where one person has sole custody, or in the cases under BEEG §4c.

Timing: Elterngeld is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid.

Whether you are entitled, and how much you receive, is decided by your Elterngeldstelle.

rows.question: Can we apply for Elterngeld online?
rows.reply:
Yes. The federal family portal says that in every Bundesland it is possible to apply for Elterngeld (parental allowance) digitally, as well as in person at an Elterngeld office. You contact the Elterngeld office responsible for the place where your child lives.

For Hessen, the portal names it among the states (with Baden-Württemberg, Bayern, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Saarland and Sachsen) where you can apply online independently of ElterngeldDigital (the federal online assistant for parental allowance applications). The excerpts do not describe how the Hessen online service works. The Elterngeld office for your child's place of residence can tell you.

ElterngeldDigital itself is offered for Berlin, Brandenburg, Bremen, Hamburg, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Niedersachsen, Rheinland-Pfalz, Sachsen-Anhalt, Schleswig-Holstein and Thüringen. There, the assistant helps you fill in the form; you then print the document, sign it, and post it to your responsible Elterngeld office.

The law says Elterngeld "ist schriftlich zu beantragen" (must be applied for in writing). The application must be signed by the person making it and, to confirm they have seen it, by the other entitled parent. This does not apply in the case of § 4c or where one person alone has custody. Elterngeld is paid retroactively for at most the three months of the child's life before the month the application is received, so a later application loses earlier months.

rows.question: Will our baby automatically be German if we are both Indian citizens?
rows.reply:
Not simply because the baby is born here. German law gives two routes to German Staatsangehörigkeit (citizenship) at birth. Whether either applies to your baby is decided by the authorities, not here.

1. Through a parent. A child acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit by birth if a parent holds German Staatsangehörigkeit ("wenn ein Elternteil die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit besitzt", StAG §4(1)). If both parents are Indian citizens, this route does not apply.

2. Through birth in Germany to foreign parents. A child of foreign parents born in Germany acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit by birth if one parent meets both of these conditions (StAG §4(3)):
- that parent has had their lawful habitual residence in Germany for five years ("seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland hat"), and
- that parent holds an unlimited right of residence ("ein unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht"), or, as a Swiss citizen or a family member of one, a residence permit under the 1999 EU–Switzerland free movement agreement.

When citizenship is acquired this way, it is entered in the birth register where the child's birth is recorded ("in dem Geburtenregister, in dem die Geburt des Kindes beurkundet ist, eingetragen").

If the baby does not become German, there is a separate residence rule (AufenthG §33). If, at the time of birth, both parents hold a residence permit, a settlement permit or an EU long-term residence permit, the child born in Germany is issued a residence permit ex officio ("von Amts wegen"). If only one parent holds one of these, a residence permit can be issued.

Whether your family meets these conditions is decided by the responsible authorities, not by this service. The excerpts do not name which office decides. For your own case, approach your local Ausländerbehörde (foreigners' authority) or the Standesamt (registry office) where the birth is registered.

rows.question: Does our newborn need a residence permit?
rows.reply:
German federal law sets out when a child born in Germany is given a residence permit. Section 33 of the Residence Act (AufenthG) attaches three rules to the parents' status at the time of birth.

1. If both parents, or the parent who alone has custody, hold a residence permit, a settlement permit or an EU long-term residence permit at the time of birth, the child born in Germany is given an Aufenthaltserlaubnis (residence permit) automatically by the authority ("wird ... die Aufenthaltserlaubnis von Amts wegen erteilt").

2. If only one parent holds one of those three permits, the child may be given an Aufenthaltserlaubnis by the authority ("kann ... von Amts wegen eine Aufenthaltserlaubnis erteilt werden"). This is a discretionary decision, not an automatic one.

3. If the mother or father holds a visa at the time of birth, or is allowed to stay without a visa, the child's stay counts as permitted until that visa or visa-free stay ends ("gilt bis zum Ablauf des Visums oder des rechtmäßigen visumfreien Aufenthalts als erlaubt").

Separately, the Nationality Act (StAG §4) sets out when a child acquires German citizenship at birth. This happens if one parent is a German citizen. It also happens for a child of foreign parents born in Germany if one parent meets two conditions. First, that parent has lawfully had their habitual residence in Germany for five years. Second, that parent holds an unlimited right of residence, or, as a Swiss citizen or a family member of one, a residence permit under the 1999 EU–Swiss agreement on free movement. The excerpts do not say how acquiring citizenship affects the need for a residence permit.

Which of these rules applies to your child depends on your and your partner's status at the time of birth. That is decided by the authority, not here. For your own case, contact your local immigration authority for where you live. The excerpts do not describe the application steps.

rows.question: We are getting Mutterschaftsgeld. Does that reduce our Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under the law, Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is set off against Elterngeld (parental allowance).

What the law counts. BEEG §3(1) lists the income that is "auf das Elterngeld angerechnet" (credited against Elterngeld). Under number 1, this includes two kinds of maternity benefit, insofar as they are due "für die Zeit ab dem Tag der Geburt des Kindes" (for the period from the day of the child's birth):
- Mutterschaftsgeld from the statutory health insurance, and
- the employer's top-up to Mutterschaftsgeld under MuSchG §20.

One payment is excluded. The one-off Mutterschaftsgeld of at most 210 euros under MuSchG §19(2) is not credited. That is the payment the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung makes to women who are not members of a statutory health insurer.

How the credit works. The 300-euro amount that is normally protected from crediting does not apply when maternity benefits under number 1 are credited (BEEG §3(2)). If the benefits are due for only part of a month of the child's life, they are credited only against the matching part of Elterngeld (BEEG §3(1)).

The official Familienportal explains the result for the same child:
- If the maternity benefits are higher than Elterngeld, you receive only the maternity benefits.
- If Elterngeld is higher, you also receive the difference as Elterngeld.
- Months in which the mother receives maternity benefits for the same child "gelten bei Ihnen als Monate mit Basiselterngeld" (count as months of Basiselterngeld). One day of entitlement in that month is enough.

The Familienportal also says that if a father takes Elterngeld while the mother is on maternity protection, the maternity benefits are not credited against his Elterngeld. They are credited only against the mother's.

Who decides. How this applies to your family, and what amount is paid, is decided by the Elterngeldstelle for your district. You can approach that office about your own case.

rows.question: Can I work while receiving Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, the law allows work while receiving Elterngeld (parental allowance), as long as it is not full-time work.

One condition of entitlement is that the person does no work or no full-time work: "keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt" (BEEG §1(1) no. 4).

The law says a person is not working full-time if any one of these applies (BEEG §1(6)):
1. their working time does not exceed 32 hours a week, averaged over the child's month of life ("32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats");
2. they are in employment for vocational training ("Beschäftigung zur Berufsbildung");
3. they work as a suitable childminder within the meaning of §§23 and 43 of Book VIII of the Social Code ("geeignete Kindertagespflegeperson").

Working affects the amount. For months after the birth in which you earn less than before the birth, Elterngeld is paid as the relevant percentage of the difference between the two incomes. For this calculation, pre-birth income counts up to at most 2,770 euros (BEEG §2(3)). The maximum of 1,800 euros a month applies to full months with no earned income (BEEG §2(1)).

The law also lets you take two months of "Elterngeld Plus" instead of one month of "Basiselterngeld" (BEEG §4(3)).

If you state in your application that you expect to earn income during the payment period, the amount is decided provisionally (BEEG §8(3) no. 3). After the payment period ends, you must prove your actual earned income for that time (BEEG §8(1)). If you stated you would have no earned income, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation if you do have earned income after all (BEEG §8(2)).

The official guidance page notes that partly different rules apply if your child was born before 1 September 2021, and refers those parents to their Elterngeldstelle.

Whether you are entitled, and how much you would receive while working, is decided only by your Elterngeldstelle.

rows.question: Where and how do we apply for Kindergeld?
rows.reply:
Where: the law says Kindergeld (child benefit) must be applied for at the competent Familienkasse ("bei der nach § 13 zuständigen Familienkasse"). This is the Familienkasse for the district where the person entitled to the benefit lives ("in deren Bezirk der Berechtigte seinen Wohnsitz hat"). If that person has no residence in Germany, it is the Familienkasse for their habitual place of stay. If they have neither, it is the one for the district where they work. In all other cases it is the Familienkasse Bayern Nord. The official family portal says to submit the application to the Familienkasse at your Agentur für Arbeit.

How: the statute says Kindergeld is to be applied for in writing ("schriftlich zu beantragen"). The family portal says the application can be made electronically or in writing, using the Familienkassen form. You can fill it in online, then print and sign it. For a newborn child, you can also submit it fully online with a valid ELSTER certificate, without printing or signing by hand. The application must include your tax identification number and your child's tax identification number.

Who applies: for each child, Kindergeld is paid to only one person. If the child lives in the parents' shared household, the parents decide between themselves who is the entitled person. If they make no decision, the family court decides on application.

Documents: for a child born or living abroad, the Federal Employment Agency asks for a copy of the foreign birth certificate, or another official document that certifies the birth. Supporting documents can be sent online to your Familienkasse. If documents are missing, the Familienkasse sets a deadline. Missing it can delay the application or lead to its rejection.

Timing: the family portal says Kindergeld can be paid retroactively for up to 6 months. Months further back are not paid.

Whether you are entitled, and to how much, is decided by the Familienkasse. For questions about applying, the Federal Employment Agency's free service line is 0800 4 555530.

rows.question: What are the Elterngeld rules for a self-employed parent in Bavaria?
rows.reply:
Bavaria is outside the states this product covers. It covers federal law, Hessen state procedures and the Indian consular track. For Bavarian procedures, such as where and how to apply, contact the office that handles Elterngeld (parental allowance) applications in Bavaria. Elterngeld itself is federal law, so the rules below apply in Bavaria too.

Who counts as working: a self-employed person who is temporarily not working still counts as employed for Elterngeld purposes ("selbständig erwerbstätig", BEEG §1(6a)). One condition for Elterngeld is that you do no work or no full-time work ("keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit", §1(1)). Under §1(6), a person is not working full time if any of these applies:
1. their working time does not exceed 32 hours a week on average over the child's month of life;
2. they are in vocational training; or
3. they work as a suitable childminder under §§23 and 43 of Book Eight of the Social Code.

Income limit: there is no entitlement if the person's taxable income in the last completed tax assessment period before the birth was more than 175,000 euros. If another person also qualifies, the limit applies to the sum of both persons' taxable income (§1(8)).

Which income counts: Elterngeld is 67 percent of income from work before the birth. This income includes positive income from "Land- und Forstwirtschaft, Gewerbebetrieb und selbständiger Arbeit" (agriculture and forestry, trade or business, and self-employed work) that is taxable in Germany. Taxes and social contributions are deducted (§2(1)).
- The percentage rises toward 100 percent where pre-birth income was below 1,000 euros. It falls toward 65 percent where that income was above 1,200 euros (§2(2)).
- The maximum is 1,800 euros a month for full months with no income from work (§2(1)).
- The minimum is 300 euros (§2(4)).
- If you earn less after the birth than before, Elterngeld is paid as the percentage of the difference. At most 2,770 euros counts as pre-birth income for this purpose (§2(3)).

Proof and provisional payment (§8):
- If the application states expected income from work, the actual income for that period must be proven after the payment period ends (§8(1)).
- If you state you expect no income from work during the payment period, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation in case you do have such income. The same applies if the tax assessment notice for the last completed period before the birth is not yet available and the application states the income limits will not be exceeded (§8(2)).
- The amount is decided provisionally, based on the information you have made credible, in any of these cases (§8(3)):
  1. the tax assessment notice for the last completed assessment period before the birth is not yet available, and it cannot yet be said whether the §1(8) limits are exceeded;
  2. pre-birth income from work cannot be determined; or
  3. you expect to have income from work during the payment period.

Whether you are entitled, and how much you would receive, is decided only by the responsible Elterngeld office in Bavaria.

rows.question: Can you fill in our Elterngeld application form for us?
rows.reply:
We cannot fill in your Elterngeld (parental allowance) application for you. Completing it means making choices and entries about your own family, and only the responsible authority decides your individual case. What we can do is set out what the law says the application must contain.

What the law requires of the application:
- It must be made in writing: "Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen" (BEEG §7(1)).
- It must state for which months of the child's life you claim the basic amount, for which months the Plus variant, and for which months the partnership bonus (BEEG §7(1)).
- It must be signed by the person applying. The other entitled parent also signs, to confirm they have seen it. This does not apply where the applicant has sole custody or in the case of §4c (BEEG §7(3)).
- The choices made in the application can be changed until the end of the payment period. Changes reach back at most three months (BEEG §7(2)).

Timing: payment is made backwards only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received: "rückwirkend nur für die letzten drei Lebensmonate" (BEEG §7(1)). Earlier months are not paid.

Documents: the federal family portal lists the child's birth certificate and proof of previous income. For employees, this means payslips for the 12 months before maternity protection begins (mothers) or before the birth (fathers). For the self-employed, it is usually the last tax assessment. Further documents may be needed depending on the individual case.

Who decides: the responsible authority is the one the Land designates for the district where the child lives at the time of the first application (BEEG §12(1)). Contact the Elterngeldstelle for your district. It decides your application.

rows.question: Based on our situation, will our Elterngeld application be approved?
rows.reply:
Whether your application will be approved is a decision about your individual case. Only the responsible authority can make it, so this answer cannot say whether you will be approved. It can set out the conditions the law attaches to Elterngeld (parental allowance).

Basic conditions (BEEG §1 Absatz 1). A person is entitled who:
1. has a residence or habitual abode in Germany ("einen Wohnsitz oder seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt in Deutschland hat"),
2. lives in one household with the child,
3. cares for and brings up the child personally, and
4. is not working, or not working full time ("keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt").
BEEG §1 Absätze 2 to 4 extend entitlement to further groups of people in particular situations.

What counts as not working full time (BEEG §1 Absatz 6). A person is not working full time if:
1. their working time does not exceed 32 hours a week on average over the child's month of life ("32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats"),
2. they are in employment for vocational training, or
3. they work as a suitable childminder within the meaning of §§ 23 and 43 SGB VIII.

Conditions for non-EU nationals (BEEG §1 Absatz 7). A foreign national without EU freedom of movement is entitled only if they:
1. hold a Niederlassungserlaubnis or an Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt-EU,
2. hold an EU Blue Card, an ICT card, a Mobile ICT card, or an Aufenthaltserlaubnis that entitles or entitled them to work for at least six months. The law excludes some permits from this: those issued for training, au pair work, seasonal work, European voluntary service, job seeking or recognition of foreign qualifications; those issued for study, recognition measures or job seeking where the person is neither working nor on Elternzeit nor receiving ongoing SGB III benefits; and humanitarian permits under § 23 Absatz 1, § 23a or § 25 Absatz 3 to 5 AufenthG,
3. hold one of those humanitarian permits and are lawfully working in Germany, on Elternzeit, or receiving ongoing SGB III benefits,
4. hold one of those humanitarian permits and have been staying in Germany lawfully, with permission or toleration for at least 15 months, or
5. hold a Beschäftigungsduldung under § 60d with § 60a Absatz 2 Satz 3 AufenthG.

Income limit (BEEG §1 Absatz 8). The entitlement lapses if the person had taxable income of more than 175,000 euros ("mehr als 175 000 Euro") in the last completed assessment period before the birth. Where another person also meets the conditions, for example the other parent in the household, the limit applies to the sum of both persons' taxable income.

The application (BEEG §7 Absatz 1). Elterngeld must be applied for in writing ("Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen"). It is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid.

The Elterngeldstelle decides whether you are entitled. Approach the Elterngeldstelle for your district.

rows.question: How much tax will we save if I switch to Steuerklasse 3 before the birth?
rows.reply:
We cannot tell you how much tax you would save by switching tax class, or whether switching makes sense for your family. Calculating tax owed or saved, and choosing a tax class, is individual tax advice. That belongs to your local tax office or a tax adviser.

What the excerpts do cover is how a tax class change before the birth is treated when the parental allowance is calculated:

- The law deducts income tax using the tax class and, where relevant, the factor under § 39f of the Income Tax Act. Tax class VI is disregarded ("die Steuerklasse VI bleibt unberücksichtigt").
- The assessment period for employment income is the twelve calendar months before the month of the birth ("die zwölf Kalendermonate vor dem Kalendermonat der Geburt des Kindes").
- If you changed tax class before the birth, the most recent tax class is used ("kommt es auf die neueste Steuerklasse an"). The older tax class is used only if it applied for longer within the whole assessment period than the newer one ("wenn diese innerhalb des gesamten Bemessungszeitraums länger gegolten hat als die neuere").
- A further change of tax class after the birth no longer affects the parental allowance.

Whether these rules mean a change helps your family, and what your parental allowance would be, is not something we can assess. The parental allowance office for your district calculates the allowance. Questions about the tax effect of a tax class change belong with your local tax office or a tax adviser.
